title: M. kansasii as a TB-mimic NTM
dek: Photochromogen that can look like pulmonary TB. Wikipedia species node. Not MTBC, not automatically HRZE.
story: M. kansasii on Wikipedia is a slow-growing photochromogen NTM famous for fibrocavitary lung disease that mimics TB. Tap water is a reservoir in many telling.
NAATs for MTBC should be negative. If a smear-positive cavity is 'TB until proven otherwise', proven otherwise is a species name.
Older regimens borrowed rifampin/INH/EMB from TB; that borrowing is IDSA-era NTM practice, not a reason to file it under tb-first-line. No doses here.
deep: Photochromogenicity is a Runyon clue, not a barcode.
rpoB sequences from kansasii will break MTBC catalogues.
TST can be positive; IGRA less so — infection-test plates.
Do not call it 'atypical TB' on a legal report. Name the species.

visual.caption: Cavity plus AFB forks into MTBC versus kansasii-like NTM. The mimic is why speciation exists.
